Thought: Cubane (C8H8) is a symmetric molecule with a cube-like structure. In C-13 NMR spectroscopy, the number of peaks corresponds to the number of chemically non-equivalent carbon environments in the molecule. To determine this, I need to analyze the structure of cubane and identify how many different types of carbon atoms it has.

Cubane has 8 carbon atoms arranged at the corners of a cube. Due to the high symmetry of the molecule, all carbon atoms are in identical chemical environments - each carbon is bonded to three other carbon atoms and one hydrogen atom. This means all carbon atoms are chemically equivalent.

When all carbon atoms are in the same chemical environment, they will produce only one signal (peak) in the C-13 NMR spectrum.
